# Pulse task #2661: Native device platform: source assessment, reusable libraries and full Live coverage roadmap

Operation: 43fe7e7af4c2daf8ed929b3a93c16844
Assignee: PORTALSURFER (Pulse #1, GitHub ID 41680373)

# Hex native device platform and Live coverage roadmap
Planning date: 17 October 2026. Destination: live Pulse, Hex project 2, version 0.1 (id 2), goal 3.
Planning only: this document authorizes no implementation, tests, merges or new delivery claims.

## Outcome and scope

Make adding a complete native device a repeatable activity: implement its original DSP and state codec, declare capabilities, compose a panel from shared UI components, register it, and pass the common lifecycle/conformance suite. New ordinary devices should not need device-specific branches in project storage, history, engine scheduling, audio callback ownership or application startup.

The product objective is native functional and workflow coverage of every device in the pinned Ableton Live Suite reference, followed by measured response/sound convergence where evidence supports it. All visible controls must have real DSP or a documented host function; defaults, ranges, modes, modulation, automation, presets, routing, bypass, discontinuities and resource limits are part of a device. A familiar name and a few working parameters do not finish it.

Version 0.1 is the requested planning container for this whole roadmap. This is not an assertion that the entire catalog is a small first release or that existing 0.2 work should move. Keep existing canonical issues and link their results.

Pin the currently documented reference to Live 12 Suite 12.4.6 (2026-09-10_0de5c8fa9a), executable SHA256 5e8832e06fe92d42ceebac4fad153e44422c90923f426dcb05c760c6d80b3949, initially macOS arm64. Recheck the installed build and browser inventory before new experiments. The current public Live 12 manual is useful inventory evidence but is a moving document, not proof that every described revision matches that installed build.

Coverage has separate statuses: catalogued; behavior specified; kernel verified; fully integrated functional device; native interaction/listening accepted; measured reference agreement. Record these per feature/mode, with source/build, fixture and tolerance. An original working implementation can advance while reference agreement remains unknown. Do not equate DSP identity with UI similarity, exact sample nulls, copied factory presets, or Live project-format import compatibility.

Include the 42 audio effects, 8 MIDI effects and 13 instruments in the current official manual; four rack types; the 18 documented stock Max for Live devices; and an audited overlay for installed first-party packs and legacy variants. Implement the stock Max devices as native Hex equivalents unless a separate explicit host decision is made. Arbitrary third-party Max patches and external plugin hosting are separate products, not a finite interpretation of “all stock devices.” Do not silently remove bundled/installed first-party devices from the coverage ledger because they are Max-based. Factory sample/IR/wavetable/preset redistribution is a separate asset inventory and provenance question; use original or appropriately licensed content.

- [registered catalog](https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/3b41e2ef07571c439b56183672ca9f747156a7c4/crates/hex-devices/src/lib.rs#L26): exactly six effects and three instruments.
- [latest neutral contract](https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/ebb55d08df4b3f777a8692940274fb2312e1c3dc/crates/hex-lattice-contract/src/lib.rs#L454): validated per-state descriptors, versioned payloads and generic edits.
- [latest lattice runtime](https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/ebb55d08df4b3f777a8692940274fb2312e1c3dc/crates/hex-lattice/src/lib.rs): mutable processors, history copying/retargeting, clocks, tails, audition, runtime caps.
- [instrument events](https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/3b41e2ef07571c439b56183672ca9f747156a7c4/crates/hex-lattice/src/instrument_runtime.rs#L35): occurrence-aware notes, channel pressure/bend/wheel, finite runtime limits.
- [widget public API](https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/3b41e2ef07571c439b56183672ca9f747156a7c4/crates/hex-widgets/src/lib.rs), [device composition](https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/3b41e2ef07571c439b56183672ca9f747156a7c4/crates/hex-ui/src/device_composition.rs), [widget ownership](https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/3b41e2ef07571c439b56183672ca9f747156a7c4/crates/hex-widgets/README.md).
- [Vector source](https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/3b41e2ef07571c439b56183672ca9f747156a7c4/crates/hex-devices/src/operator_state.rs), [Vector globals](https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/3b41e2ef07571c439b56183672ca9f747156a7c4/docs/vector-global.md), [current state](https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/3b41e2ef07571c439b56183672ca9f747156a7c4/docs/operator-state.md).
- Device-specific bounded claims: docs/utility-filters.md, eq-eight.md, saturator.md, compressor.md, gate.md, auto-pan.md.
- Existing host seams: docs/device-gestures.md, device-presets.md, device-gain-staging.md, spectrum-analysis.md, routing.md, lattice-instruments.md, performance.md.
- Official reference inventory: [audio effects](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-audio-effect-reference/), [MIDI effects](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-midi-effect-reference/), [instruments](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/), [racks](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/instrument-drum-and-effect-racks/), [stock Max devices](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/max-for-live-devices/), inspected 17 October 2026.

Documentation drift is material. docs/features.md and portions of operator-native.md/operator-waveforms.md describe historical limitations already superseded by source and newer docs. For example, Vector globals are implemented, not decorative local UI; the historical 16-voice feedback path is not the only current runtime. Preserve historical evidence but label its source/version and update current summaries.

## What already exists, and what still needs work

| Area | Verified foundation | Remaining platform work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Registry/state | Six effects: Utility, EQ8, Saturator, Compressor, Gate, Auto Pan. Sine, FM4, Vector instruments. Stable IDs, opaque versioned codec, generic project/history/storage, bounded parameter snapshots. PR273 adds state-aware validated descriptors. | Declarative capabilities, stable dynamic-instance parameter identity, common authoring fixtures, event/port/asset references, automation/modulation policy. |
| DSP runtime | Analytic and mutable instruments, prepared processors, clock access, compatible history, transactional twins, explicit tails/quiescence, bounded publication and control-side reclamation. | Efficient large mutable histories for delay/reverb/FFT/sample devices; aggregate memory/admission policies; complete transport/live-edit behavior by capability. |
| Resource limits | 4 KiB authored device-state payload, 512 descriptors, 64-entry compound edit; latest per-effect twin cap 64 KiB; aggregate host limits remain separate. | Keep sample/IR/table assets out of small payloads. Audit snapshot/list/memory limits against real devices. Raising one cap alone does not make large-buffer DSP viable. |
| Vector | State v15, 1,728 bytes, 424 descriptors; harmonic editing, companion envelopes/filter/LFO, eleven algorithms, global/controller assignments, 1–32 selected voices, 2x quality path. Legacy patches preserve legacy processing. | Full reference parameter/mode audit and measured laws; MIDI/MPE depth; dense performance. Current new runtime is 116,520 bytes/twin, 233,040 bytes/pair against the 2 MiB aggregate DSP-pair pool. |
| Shared UI | GPUI knobs/sliders/readouts, toggles/selectors/popups, graphs, harmonic bars, meter strips, frame/header/sections/layout, persistent entities and gesture phases. Shared production composition and gallery, unified theme. | Reusable host binding adapter; advanced waveform/sample-zone/rack/modulation/spectrogram/algorithm widgets; accessibility; catalog-scale browsing and panel lifecycle. Extend existing libraries. |
| Gestures/presets | Bounded Begin/Change/Commit/Cancel, coalescing, one undo transaction, preview/canonical/applied separation, save/export barriers. User preset save/load exists. | Reuse these for every control and multi-parameter editor. Extend asset-aware presets/racks, migrations, mappings and applied-state feedback; no second edit model. |
| Host routing | Typed Track/Return audio routing, authored MIDI source routing, sends, latency accumulation/compensation, shared capture/export. | Device sidechains/aux ports, audio-effect MIDI inputs, per-device multioutputs, nested racks, external hardware. Preserve existing compensation rather than rebuild it. |
| Events/modulation | Sample-offset occurrence-aware instrument notes and logical-channel expression; device-local LFO/controller logic. | MIDI-effect chain, generated-note ownership, per-note MPE, sustain/CC as required, common automation/modulation evaluation and scale/tempo context. |
| Analysis/assets | EQ8 analyzer and meters use bounded backend telemetry; WAV/media/stream/warp infrastructure exists. | General analysis views and calibrated meters; sample instruments, IR/wavetable device assets, real-time granular/FFT modules. Existing offline warp or analyzer code is not automatically a real-time processor. |
| Quality | Extensive focused DSP/PCM/storage/history/rendered GPUI/allocation tests and measured profiles. | Common registry-driven conformance, per-device acceptance records, reproducible physical deadlines, sustained catalog workloads, source-linked reference captures. No new acceptance claimed by this audit. |

Existing limited effects are useful originals, not full clones. Saturator has two original curves and no oversampling/color section; Compressor lacks reference lookahead/sidechain/detector/RMS/auto modes in the audited slice; Gate lacks sidechain/detector filter/lookahead; Auto Pan is a three-parameter free-running sine modulator rather than the modern full Auto Pan–Tremolo. EQ8 has substantial multibank/filter/graph/analyzer support; #2654 is its active dynamic-band/automation owner. Utility needs a pinned reference control/transfer-law audit, not another basic gain implementation.

## Chosen architecture and library boundaries

1. **hex-lattice-contract remains the neutral authored contract.** Stable device/parameter/subobject IDs, versioned state, state-aware descriptors, declared capabilities and neutral asset/port references. It must not depend on DSP, GPUI, project editing or filesystem I/O. Authored state, runtime state, editor state and telemetry are distinct.
2. **hex-lattice remains the native processing protocol.** Prepared immutable configurations, effect/instrument/MIDI-process contracts, input context, resource declarations, lifecycle/history/tail/latency semantics. Keep dispatch and registration cheap and bounded. Add optional typed capabilities instead of one giant trait requiring every device to fake support.
3. **Create hex-dsp when extracting the first shared production kernels.** Own safe, independently testable math/blocks only: units/conversions, smoothing, oscillators/noise, envelopes/LFOs, filters/detectors, delay/interpolation, oversampling, FFT/windowing, convolution, resampling, spectral/pitch and physical-model building blocks. No project, files, queues, registry or UI dependencies. Move only proven shared kernels, retaining original-law golden fixtures; do not create a speculative empty library or force a universal mega-processor.
4. **hex-devices owns named device algorithms/codecs/presentation metadata.** Modules or family crates are split when independent responsibility/build cost warrants it, not one crate per knob. Device-specific nonlinear laws remain here even when composed from shared DSP. No host routing/scheduling/storage branches.
5. **hex-widgets remains generic native rendering and interaction.** Theme values/text are injected; DSP and parameter meaning remain outside. Add waveform, zone, matrix, XY and other controls only when a concrete device needs them.
6. **A device UI layer separates reusable binding/composition from the application.** First extract a small host adapter/module from hex-ui/device_panel; promote to hex-device-ui when Utility plus a complex device use it independently. Its permitted dependencies are GPUI, hex-widgets and neutral lattice contracts. It accepts canonical/draft/applied snapshots, normalized preview data and typed edit/navigation callbacks. hex-ui owns project/selection/command adaptation, not the new library. Specialized panel modules are legitimate; generic fallback remains available. Avoid a giant declarative template with device-name switches inside widgets.
7. **hex-project/session/engine/audio retain host ownership.** Project owns authored routing/automation/racks; session validates edits and coordinates workers; engine compiles the graph and deterministic event/automation/render order; audio owns CPAL/queues/telemetry transport; media/stream/storage own assets/I/O; desktop composes. Reuse the same processor graph and clock semantics for Arrangement, Session, monitoring and expo

Planning date: 17 October 2026. Destination: live Pulse, Hex project 2, version 0.1 (id 2), goal 3.
Planning only: this document authorizes no implementation, tests, merges or new delivery claims.

## Outcome and scope

Make adding a complete native device a repeatable activity: implement its original DSP and state codec, declare capabilities, compose a panel from shared UI components, register it, and pass the common lifecycle/conformance suite. New ordinary devices should not need device-specific branches in project storage, history, engine scheduling, audio callback ownership or application startup.

The product objective is native functional and workflow coverage of every device in the pinned Ableton Live Suite reference, followed by measured response/sound convergence where evidence supports it. All visible controls must have real DSP or a documented host function; defaults, ranges, modes, modulation, automation, presets, routing, bypass, discontinuities and resource limits are part of a device. A familiar name and a few working parameters do not finish it.

Version 0.1 is the requested planning container for this whole roadmap. This is not an assertion that the entire catalog is a small first release or that existing 0.2 work should move. Keep existing canonical issues and link their results.

Pin the currently documented reference to Live 12 Suite 12.4.6 (2026-09-10_0de5c8fa9a), executable SHA256 5e8832e06fe92d42ceebac4fad153e44422c90923f426dcb05c760c6d80b3949, initially macOS arm64. The current public Live 12 manual is useful inventory evidence but is a moving document, not proof that every described revision matches that installed build.

Coverage has separate statuses: catalogued; behavior specified; kernel verified; fully integrated functional device; native interaction/listening accepted; measured reference agreement. Record these per feature/mode, with source/build, fixture and tolerance. An original working implementation can advance while reference agreement remains unknown. Do not equate DSP identity with UI similarity, exact sample nulls, copied factory presets, or Live project-format import compatibility.

Include the 42 audio effects, 8 MIDI effects and 13 instruments in the current official manual; four rack types; the 18 documented stock Max for Live devices; and an audited overlay for installed first-party packs and legacy variants. Implement the stock Max devices as native Hex equivalents unless a separate explicit host decision is made. ## Chosen architecture and library boundaries

1. **hex-lattice-contract remains the neutral authored contract.** Stable device/parameter/subobject IDs, versioned state, state-aware descriptors, declared capabilities and neutral asset/port references. It must not depend on DSP, GPUI, project editing or filesystem I/O. Authored state, runtime state, editor state and telemetry are distinct.
2. **hex-lattice remains the native processing protocol.** Prepared immutable configurations, effect/instrument/MIDI-process contracts, input context, resource declarations, lifecycle/history/tail/latency semantics. Keep dispatch and registration cheap and bounded. Add optional typed capabilities instead of one giant trait requiring every device to fake support.
